description: A responsive playbook editor for American football defensive coordinators to design, adjust, annotate, organize, and export defensive plays.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?
questions.rationale: The existing Vite starter uses React JSX and JavaScript.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Continue the existing JSX starter with JavaScript.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and UI approach should be used?
questions.recommendedChoice: React 19 with native responsive SVG and React pointer events
questions.answer: React 19 with native responsive SVG and React pointer events
questions.rationale: The existing frontend is React 19 on Vite; native SVG keeps play data predictable and editable.

options.label: React 19 with native responsive SVG and React pointer events
options.description: Use the existing React/Vite app and SVG field editor; add lucide-react for controls.

options.label: React with react-konva
options.description: Canvas-oriented interaction model for a later performance or freehand phase.

options.label: Other
options.description: Provide an alternative framework or rendering approach.

questions.question: What should the frontend deliver in the first implementation?
questions.recommendedChoice: Responsive playboard editor with 11v11, 7v7, and 4v4 presets; base plays and named formation-adjustment slides; symbol players; routes, blitzes, zones, man indicators, alignments, responsibilities, annotations; drag/select/delete/clear; undo/redo; searchable play library foundations; and print-ready PDF export for one play or a whole playbook.
questions.answer: Responsive playboard editor with 11v11, 7v7, and 4v4 presets; base plays and named formation-adjustment slides; symbol players; routes, blitzes, zones, man indicators, alignments, responsibilities, annotations; drag/select/delete/clear; undo/redo; searchable play library foundations; and print-ready PDF export for one play or a whole playbook.
questions.rationale: These capabilities are explicitly required for the first product direction, with scouting/video analysis and practice scheduling deferred.

questions.question: Which language should the backend use?
questions.rationale: The existing API is an Azure Functions Python app.

options.label: Python
options.description: Continue the existing Azure Functions Python app.

questions.question: Which backend framework and API approach should be used?
questions.recommendedChoice: Azure Functions Python v2 programming model with an HTTP API and storage abstraction
questions.answer: Azure Functions Python v2 programming model with an HTTP API and storage abstraction
questions.rationale: The existing function_app.py already uses the Azure Functions Python v2 model; the storage boundary supports Azurite now and Azure later.

options.label: Azure Functions Python v2 programming model with an HTTP API and storage abstraction
options.description: Implement authenticated playbook and export APIs behind repository/service boundaries.

questions.question: What should the backend deliver in the first implementation?
questions.recommendedChoice: Authenticated play and playbook CRUD with ownership and coordinator/owner, assistant/editor, and viewer authorization; slide/version persistence; search and metadata foundations; export job/data endpoints; local development identity behind an explicit development flag and local secret; and Azurite-compatible storage adapters.
questions.answer: Authenticated play and playbook CRUD with ownership and coordinator/owner, assistant/editor, and viewer authorization; slide/version persistence; search and metadata foundations; export job/data endpoints; local development identity behind an explicit development flag and local secret; and Azurite-compatible storage adapters.
questions.rationale: The API must enforce authentication and play ownership; no plaintext passwords or Google credentials may be stored.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores are required?
sharedQuestions.rationale: Use Azurite-compatible Table Storage for structured playbook data and Blob Storage for PDF exports/assets, with an abstraction for future Azure services.

options.label: Azure Table Storage
options.description: Structured local/Azure-compatible playbook, membership, metadata, and revision records.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: PDF exports, uploaded assets, and future media-backed artifacts.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in to access application API features?
sharedQuestions.rationale: Individual coach authentication and server-side ownership enforcement are required; prefer Microsoft Entra External ID with Google federation, with Auth0 or Clerk as alternatives.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require external OIDC authentication and enforce roles and ownership in the Python API.
